name: Retro Shiva: Persinger Session run clockwise (Murphy's reading)
origin: Todd Murphy (Shiva 'Persinger Session'); 'Retro Shiva' after an unsigned practitioner's testimonial on Murphy's Shiva page (by 2011), placed with the page's link to the DeepFocus Institute, read as clockwise running by Murphy (2013), who credits the Swiss DeepFocus group (Rolf Boesch)
summary: The Shiva 'Persinger Session' (seven applications of a 40 Hz 'chirp' with silences between them, about 43 min) run clockwise instead of counter-clockwise, which is how Murphy reads the 'Retro Shiva' of a practitioner's testimonial. The practitioner, who works mainly with healers and energy workers, tried it for people 'not able to come out of their energy state'; Murphy says the Swiss DeepFocus group found that running Shiva 'backwards' can ease 'the mental fatigue that can come from too much spiritual work'.
notes: The Persinger Session (the timing of murphy-shiva-persinger-session) run clockwise. Where the idea comes from: an unsigned testimonial on Murphy's Shiva page, archived in 2011, sits in one block that ends with the page's link to 'Research at the DeepFocus Institute', so it is attributed to the DeepFocus practitioner (it promises 'a article about this topic'); it says 'I tried a new application with Shiva: The "Retro Shiva" in which I turn the cap and apply the 40hz Chirp Signal (Persinger session)'; later versions of the page insert '(around)' after 'turn the cap', and the testimonial never mentions clockwise rotation. Murphy's 2013 blog reads it as running Shiva 'backwards', 'using clockwise rotation around the head instead of the usual counterclockwise configuration', and credits the Swiss group. The clockwise reading is Murphy's, not the user's words, and it is geometrically open: turning a ring cap 180 degrees about the vertical axis keeps the counter-clockwise stepping and only moves the first coil to the back of the head (that reading is simply murphy-shiva-persinger-session started at O2); only a mirror-image fitting (the cap flipped over) or a reversed channel order steps clockwise. This file follows Murphy's clockwise reading. Coils sit on Murphy's Shiva ring, one coil per site instead of Shiva's coil pairs, and step clockwise seen from above, starting at Fp2, the mirror image of Shiva's usual first coil over the left frontal area (a project choice): Fp2, FT8, TP8, O2, O1, TP7, FT7, Fp1 (front to back on the right, back to front on the left). Murphy gives only 'seven unique applications of the chirp signal with silent sections in between ... about 43 minutes'; no source gives the length of each application or silence, so the split into 7 x 5 min with 80-s silences is a project choice. The chirp file is proprietary. Murphy says it 'does not change in tone, but rather has longer and longer gaps between sections of the signal as they travel around your head', so a steady 40 Hz carrier is used and the coil-to-coil timing supplies the gaps; the 40 Hz modulation of the original is not reproduced. Each block has its own dwell ramp (a project assignment): blocks 1-6 step +2 ms per coil, from Murphy's lecture example of 10 to 20 ms up to 20 to 30 ms (six values, so these ramps restart every six coils instead of lining up with the eight positions); block 7 uses the lab Octopus ramp, +20 ms per coil from 20 to 160 ms, then reset (Richards 2002). Murphy's other statements of the Shiva speed ('around 9 times per second'; in 2007 'around the same speed' as the 25-ms binding factor) do not match the lecture example, and the real Shiva timing tables are unpublished. The lab Octopus used about 1-10 µT; this file defaults to 1 µT, and the vendor advises starting at 50% volume and raising it over sessions. Persinger's lab reported more left-hemisphere power with clockwise and more right-hemisphere power with counter-clockwise rotation (Booth, Koren & Persinger 2008, not independently replicated); Murphy's suggestion that running Shiva 'backwards' may enhance 'left-hemispheric spiritual practices (like those that rely on prayer and work towards joy and light)' goes beyond that result. The reported benefits are testimonials: the practitioner says the clients felt clearer and more structured, and one Kriya-yoga user found the light of his practice 'stronger' with clockwise sessions (Murphy: 'only one case'). Murphy's blog calls the Swiss work 'an independent replication' led by 'Dr. Rolf Bosch'; the German report behind it ('Elektronische Erleuchtung?', Rolf Boesch, Institut für mediale Entwicklung, archived July 2011) is a two-page testimonial of 400 test sessions in Germany and Switzerland, mostly with the Persinger Session, that asserts EEG findings without data, methods or controls and mentions neither clockwise nor 'retro' use. Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Murphy calls counter-clockwise 'usually the more pleasant direction': if the clockwise run feels unpleasant, stop. Not for people with epilepsy; stop at once if distressed. Revised Oct 2026 after a re-check of the sources: the testimonial's original wording ('turn the cap', with '(around)' added later), its unsigned author (attributed by the page layout to the DeepFocus practitioner) and the 180-degree-turn alternative were added, and the clockwise reading is now credited to Murphy rather than to the Swiss report; the phase names were shortened; the timing and rotation are unchanged.
setting: Dark, quiet room, eyes closed, seated or lying relaxed. For the Persinger Session Murphy advises against spiritual practice or psychic exercises during the session ('daydreaming is better than meditation') and suggests geomagnetically quiet days for effects during the session.
schedule: At most once a week, like the counter-clockwise Persinger Session. Murphy says the Swiss averaged 4 sessions per subject; their German report speaks of about 100 people with five or more sessions.
